title: Squad Atlas (Payments) Onboarding
description: Week-one essentials for new engineers joining Meridian's Squad Atlas — on-call, compliance, releases, data, architecture, and secrets.

questions.prompt: Which tool does Squad Atlas use to run its on-call rotation and page the primary engineer?
questions.explanation: Atlas runs its on-call rotation through Opsgenie; keep the app installed on your phone and test push notifications before your first shift (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: When an Atlas alert fires, how long does the primary on-call engineer have to acknowledge it before Opsgenie escalates?
questions.explanation: Alerts route to the primary on-call with a 10-minute acknowledgement SLA; missing it escalates to the secondary, then the squad lead (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: On Squad Atlas, a failed payment settlement is classified as which incident severity?
questions.explanation: Severity is set by impact to money movement: a failed settlement impacts money movement, so it is Sev1 — never downgrade it to Sev2 because 'only a few payments' failed (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: Because Atlas handles cardholder data directly, under which compliance regime does the squad operate?
questions.explanation: As Meridian's highest-volume card processor, Atlas operates under PCI-DSS Level 1 — the strictest tier — and every engineer completes PCI awareness training before production access (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: How is card data classified in Meridian's data tiers as handled by Squad Atlas?
questions.explanation: Card data is Tier 0 (Restricted), Meridian's highest data tier: it may never be logged, never appear in error messages, and never leave the boundary of PCI-scope services (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: What does Squad Atlas's release policy say about when production deploys may happen?
choices: Deploys allowed any day during business hours
No deploys on Friday or over the weekend
Deploys only during a nightly release window
questions.explanation: Because Atlas runs money movement, the pipeline is gated to refuse production releases Friday through Sunday; a fix that truly can't wait goes through the incident-change path with on-call lead plus Priya sign-off (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: How many approvals does every Atlas production change require before release?
choices: Dual approval — two engineers, one with context on the area
Approval from the squad lead only
Three approvals including a security reviewer
questions.explanation: Every production change needs dual approval, and one of the two approvers must have context on the area changed — a rubber-stamp from someone unfamiliar with the ledger does not count (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: Which mandatory check must pass before any Atlas pull request can merge?
questions.explanation: The ledger-reconciliation contract test must be green before merge — it verifies that recorded entries match settled balances. A red result blocks merge with no exceptions and no override (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: What is Squad Atlas's primary datastore for the ledger?
questions.explanation: The primary datastore is Aurora PostgreSQL, modeled as an append-only ledger — strong consistency for balance reads and the durability money movement demands (Squad Atlas — Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: How is the Atlas ledger modeled in its datastore?
choices: Append-only — corrections are new offsetting entries, rows are never updated or deleted
Event-sourced with periodic snapshots replacing history
questions.explanation: The ledger is append-only: rows are never updated or deleted in place, corrections are new entries that offset prior ones, so the full history is reconstructable — this is what makes reconciliation and audit possible (Squad Atlas — Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: What is the name of Squad Atlas's primary service and repository?
questions.explanation: atlas-ledger-svc is the primary service and repo where the ledger, settlement workers, and reconciliation logic live — new hires should clone it first (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership / Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: What is the internal codename for Atlas's payment-initiation API?
questions.explanation: Rail is the internal name for the payment-initiation endpoint on atlas-ledger-svc; 'submit it to Rail' means hand a payment instruction to the entry point that validates and records it (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership / Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: Who is Squad Atlas's squad lead and engineering manager?
questions.explanation: Priya Nair is the squad lead and EM, and the escalation point for ownership disputes, hiring, and cross-squad commitments touching the payment path — book a week-one 1:1 with her (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership).

questions.prompt: Where does Squad Atlas store all of its secrets?
choices: AWS Secrets Manager, tagged per service
Vault, under a dedicated per-squad namespace 'atlas/'
Encrypted .env files committed to each repo
A shared org-wide Vault root path
questions.explanation: All Atlas secrets live in Vault under the dedicated per-squad namespace 'atlas/'; nothing belonging to Atlas is stored outside it, and services read from 'atlas/' at runtime rather than copying secrets into code (Squad Atlas — Secrets & Access).

questions.prompt: What customer-facing SLA does Squad Atlas publish for payment status availability?
questions.explanation: Atlas publishes a customer-facing SLA of 99.95% monthly for payment status availability; breaching it triggers a customer-facing comms review, so the status path is treated as a first-class concern (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership).
